title: openai/codex-security: a scanner for your own repo, with a spend limit
friendlyTitle: Codex Security scans your own code and can stop when the budget runs out
summary: Codex Security is OpenAI's command-line tool and TypeScript kit for scanning a codebase, checking whether a reported weakness is real, and proposing a fix. Release 0.9.1 shipped on 10 November. A commit on 11 November keeps a scan's budget across retries. It gained 20 stars on GitHub's daily trending list, with 11,611 in total. It is published on npm as @openai/codex-security.
friendlySummary: Codex Security is OpenAI's tool for scanning a code project, checking whether a reported weakness is real, and suggesting a fix. Version 0.9.1 came out on 10 November. A change on 11 November keeps the scan inside a spending limit, including retries. It gained 20 stars on GitHub's daily list and has 11,611 in total.
whyItMatters: Use it to review a repository you own before you merge, and to cap what the scan is allowed to spend. A proposed fix is a draft. You still read the diff. It is not a reason to point an agent at a system you do not control. Twenty stars in a day is a small move on a large repo. The useful change this week is the budget, not the star count.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Use it on a project you own, before you merge, and set a limit on what the scan can spend. A suggested fix is a draft. You still read the change. Do not point it at a system you do not control. The useful update this week is the spending limit, not the star count.
